intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like msemen flatbreads, harira soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the towering golden dunes of the Sahara at sunset, then spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine and mint tea, listen to Gnawa music, and wake up to a spectacular desert sunrise.

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the 16th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, the ornate Bahia Palace, and the vibrant souks where artisans craft leather goods, spices, ceramics, and lanterns using centuries-old techniques.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a sandboard and carve your way down the dramatic slopes of the Erg Chebbi dunes for an adrenaline-pumping desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction, making it accessible for beginners while still thrilling for experienced riders. Combine with quad biking for extra excitement.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen where a local chef teaches you to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla. The experience typically begins with a guided visit to the spice market to select fresh ingredients.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-70 MAD) to your riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: First walk around Djemaa el-Fna square to soak in the atmosphere — snake charmers, musicians, and street performers. Stroll into the nearby souks (Souk Semmarine) for a gentle introduction to Marrakech's labyrinthine markets. No pressure to buy — just explore and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at dusk when the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch the spectacle from a rooftop café terrace (Café de France or Café Argana) with a fresh orange juice (~4 MAD). Spend the evening wandering and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna: harira soup (7 MAD), msemen flatbread (5 MAD), or a sandwich from a local stall.
meals.dinner: Eat at one of the numbered food stalls in Djemaa el-Fna square — grilled brochettes, kefta, and bread for ~40-60 MAD. Point and choose — stall numbers 1-10 are popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash at the airport or an ATM in the Medina (avoid airport exchange desks for best rates). Keep your valuables close in the souks. Negotiate all taxi fares before getting in.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims, free) — the minaret is stunning at sunrise. Then walk to the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Bahia Palace (~10 MAD entry) — a lavish 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, explore the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and its covered market. Stop at Place des Ferblantiers for a rest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD) — one of North Africa's largest Islamic schools, with stunning zellige tilework and carved stucco. Explore the northern Medina souks by lamplight — the spice souk and lantern souk are magical after dark.

meals.breakfast: Café Clock or a local café near the riad: mint tea, msemen, and amlou (argan oil dip) for ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Chez Lamine near the Saadian Tombs — a local favorite for mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) served by weight, ~50-70 MAD.
meals.dinner: Neighbourhood restaurant in the Medina — try a tagine with bread at a local spot away from the main square for ~50-60 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are cobblestoned and uneven. A combined ticket for several monuments may save money. Madrasa and Saadian Tombs can be bundled for a slight discount.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Atlas Mountains and Berber villages — book a shared group tour from your riad or a local agency (budget ~150-200 MAD per person). Visit Imlil village, the gateway to Jebel Toubkal (North Africa's highest peak). Walk through terraced fields and meet local Berber families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the tour to the Ourika Valley — a lush river valley with waterfalls (seasonal). Trek to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (~1-2 hours round trip, easy trail). Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery and cool air — a refreshing contrast to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by late afternoon/early evening. Relax at your riad. Visit a traditional hammam near Djemaa el-Fna for a budget scrub and steam session — Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~50-80 MAD for basic service).

meals.breakfast: At your riad or a local café: khobz bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (~20 MAD).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local bakery or eat at a Berber restaurant in Imlil/Ourika Valley — fresh tagine with mountain views (~60-80 MAD).
meals.dinner: Simple dinner near the riad — a bowl of harira soup and chebakia pastry from a street stall (~20-30 MAD). Rest up for tomorrow.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Atlas/Ourika tour the night before through your riad to get the best rate — group shared tours are the most budget-friendly option. Bring a light jacket as mountain temperatures can be cooler than Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~6:00-7:00 AM) by shared CTM bus or a pre-booked shared minivan toward Merzouga/Sahara (~9-10 hours total journey, ~150-200 MAD by bus via Ouarzazate). The route crosses the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) — stunning scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') — visit the Kasbah Taourirt (entry ~20 MAD), a UNESCO-listed mud-brick fortress. Explore the Atlas Film Studios exterior (free from outside). Grab lunch and continue the journey southeast toward the Draa Valley and Zagora.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Merzouga or M'Hamid by evening. Check into a budget desert camp or basic guesthouse (~150-200 MAD per night). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire under an impossibly star-filled sky. Drummers and music are often part of the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure — bread, jam, and tea.
meals.lunch: Stop in Ouarzazate for a simple restaurant lunch — a chicken tagine or omelette with bread (~50-60 MAD).
meals.dinner: Included in most desert camp packages — Berber couscous or tagine cooked over a fire (~included or ~80 MAD separately).

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared transport and desert camp in advance through your riad or a budget agency. The Tizi n'Tichka pass road is winding — take motion sickness tablets if needed. Bring warm layers as desert nights drop significantly in temperature, especially in March.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (5:30 AM) for a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes to watch the sunrise — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences (~100-150 MAD for a 1-2 hour camel ride, often included in camp packages). Climb a dune barefoot for panoramic desert views. The golden light at sunrise is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest during the hottest midday hours at camp. Explore the edge of the dune sea on foot or by quad bike (optional, ~150-200 MAD extra). Visit the nearby village of Merzouga — browse fossil and mineral shops (Morocco's Sahara is rich in prehistoric fossils). Visit a local Gnawa musician family if the camp arranges it.
day_by_day.evening: Second sunset camel ride or dune walk. Enjoy another campfire dinner under the stars. Participate in a Berber drumming and music circle — a deeply memorable cultural experience. Sleep in a traditional nomad-style tent with blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at camp before the sunrise trek — dates, bread, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Camp lunch — tagine, salad, and bread (usually included in camp package or ~60 MAD).
meals.dinner: Campfire Berber dinner — harira, tagine, and sweet mint tea. Often included in camp package.

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the trip — embrace the silence and scale of the desert. Bring a headscarf or shemagh to protect from sand. Charge all devices as electricity may be limited at camp. March temperatures are ideal — warm days (~25°C) and cool nights (~8-12°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from the desert back toward Marrakech via a different scenic southern route through the Draa Valley — passing ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and ksour (fortified villages). Stop at Aït Benhaddou (entry ~20 MAD), the most famous ksar in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage Site used in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend 1-2 hours exploring Aït Benhaddou's mud-brick towers and labyrinthine alleys. Cross the river on stepping stones to reach the main ksar. Continue the journey back toward Marrakech, passing through Ouarzazate again. The landscape transitions dramatically from desert to mountain.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (~6-7 PM). Return to your riad. Head to Djemaa el-Fna for a final evening in the square — enjoy the storytellers, acrobats, and musicians. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer Medina restaurant to celebrate the desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Dates, bread, and tea at the desert camp before departure.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop near Aït Benhaddou — a simple tagine at a local restaurant (~50-60 MAD).
meals.dinner: Restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna — try pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or a full lamb tagine with preserved lemon (~80-100 MAD for a slightly elevated budget meal).

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is a must-stop — don't rush it. The drive back over the Tizi n'Tichka pass at sunset is spectacular. If you're exhausted, ask your transport to drop you directly at the Medina gate nearest your riad.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~70 MAD, or ~170 MAD with Yves Saint Laurent Museum). The cobalt-blue villa and exotic botanical garden are stunning in morning light. Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. The adjacent Berber Museum (included in ticket) showcases Amazigh jewelry, clothing, and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souk shopping in the Medina — pick up budget souvenirs: argan oil, spices, leather goods, lanterns, or Berber rugs. Practice your bargaining (start at 30-40% of the asking price). Visit the Cooperative Artisanale de Marrakech for fixed-price crafts if you prefer not to negotiate. Pack your bags and check out of the riad.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time — enjoy a final mint tea and pastry at a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna. Take a final stroll through the square at dusk. Head to the airport (petit taxi ~50-70 MAD, allow 30-40 minutes). Carry home memories of kasbahs, dunes, and the call to prayer echoing across the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast or café near Majorelle — avocado toast or msemen with honey and mint tea (~25-35 MAD).
meals.lunch: Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina (mid-range, ~80-100 MAD) or a final street food spread at Djemaa el-Fna — brochettes, olives, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~40 MAD).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a light snack before departure — grab a final Moroccan sandwich or pastry to take with you (~20-30 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden sells out of timed entry slots — book online in advance (jardinmajorelle.com) to guarantee entry. Budget approximately 2,500-3,500 MAD (~$250-350 USD) total for the full 7-day trip excluding flights, covering accommodation, transport, entry fees, food, and a camel ride. Morocco in March is ideal — warm, dry, and pre-peak-season prices.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a petit taxi or pre-arranged transfer (~80–120 MAD) to your riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll around Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding souks. Explore the nearby Rue des Épices and the spice market to acclimatize to the sights, sounds, and smells of Marrakech. Visit the Ben Youssef Mosque exterior and the historic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (entry free, exterior viewing).
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical transformation of Djemaa el-Fna at dusk — snake charmers, musicians, storytellers, and food stalls light up the square. Enjoy a mint tea from a rooftop café overlooking the square (Café de France or Café Argana offer great views).

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack at your riad upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at a café near the riad — try msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with honey and argan oil at a local café (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dine at one of the food stalls in Djemaa el-Fna for an authentic and affordable experience — try harira soup, merguez sandwiches, and fresh orange juice (~80–120 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep cash in small denominations for food stalls and taxis. The Medina can be disorienting — download an offline map (Maps.me or Google Maps offline). Dress modestly out of respect for local customs. Stay hydrated as March can still be warm (~20–25°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Then walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace offering panoramic views from its terraces. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Afterward, wander through the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and browse the antique and jewelry shops along its narrow alleys.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Djemaa el-Fna and explore the vibrant souks — the leather souk, lantern souk, and textile souk are all within walking distance. Practice your bargaining skills. End the evening with a traditional dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad (usually included) — expect Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Rahba Lakdima) — a stylish rooftop spot with modern Moroccan cuisine (~150–200 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina — a beautiful courtyard setting with traditional tagines and couscous (~200–280 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Bahia Palace tickets in advance during peak season. Wear comfortable walking shoes — cobblestone streets can be uneven. A guided walking tour of the Mellah (~200–300 MAD) can add great historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD, Yves Saint Laurent Museum extra ~100 MAD) — a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden filled with exotic plants, fountains, and the fascinating Berber Museum. Arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD), housed in a magnificent 19th-century palace, featuring Moroccan art and artifacts. Then explore the Ben Youssef Medersa (entry ~70 MAD), a 14th-century Islamic college with breathtaking carved plasterwork and cedar wood — one of Morocco's most beautiful architectural gems.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech (~300–500 MAD for a full gommage scrub and massage). A perfect way to relax after two days of sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif near the Majorelle Garden area — healthy wraps, salads, and Moroccan plates (~120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Al Fassia restaurant — renowned for authentic Moroccan cuisine run entirely by women, excellent pastilla and tagines (~250–350 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially for evening slots. The Majorelle Garden is very photogenic — bring your camera. The YSL Museum is optional but highly recommended for design and fashion enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (6:30–7:00 AM) by shared or private 4x4 transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the scenic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel on foot (~1.5–2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Drâa Valley with its vast palm groves and kasbahs. Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') — optional quick stop at the Atlas Film Studios exterior. Continue toward Agdz and Zagora, arriving at the edge of the Sahara by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute ride into the Erg Chigaga or Erg Lihoudi dunes. Arrive at a mid-range desert camp with private Berber tents, traditional rugs, and lanterns. Watch the sunset paint the dunes gold and enjoy an unforgettable stargazing experience in total darkness.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Aït Benhaddou — try a lamb tagine or vegetable couscous (~80–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around a campfire with live Gnawa music (~included in camp package or ~200–300 MAD separately)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~7–8 hours total with stops). A shared group transfer costs ~400–600 MAD per person; a private 4x4 with driver costs ~1,200–1,800 MAD. Pack a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara — an absolutely unmissable, awe-inspiring experience. Optional sandboarding down the dunes (~50–100 MAD equipment rental). Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the desert camp and begin the return journey. Stop at Drâa Valley oases for photos and a short walk through a palm grove with a local guide. Visit the Kasbah Amridil near Skoura — one of Morocco's most photographed kasbahs, surrounded by a sea of palm trees.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Ouarzazate area by late afternoon. Check into a mid-range kasbah hotel (such as Dar Ahlam area guesthouses or Kasbah Hida, ~500–900 MAD/night). Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll through Ouarzazate town and visit the Taourirt Kasbah (entry ~20 MAD) at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — khobz bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in the Drâa Valley — fresh salads, tagine, and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your kasbah hotel or a local restaurant in Ouarzazate — try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or chicken with preserved lemon (~150–220 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise in the Sahara is the highlight of the entire trip — set multiple alarms! Sandboarding is suitable for all fitness levels. If budget allows, a short sunrise hot air balloon ride over the dunes can be arranged in advance (~1,500–2,500 MAD).

day_by_day.morning: Drive back to Marrakech via the High Atlas Mountains (Tizi n'Tichka pass). Stop at a Berber village along the way for a authentic mint tea with a local family (many guesthouses along the route offer this). Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery — snow-capped peaks in March are common and spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Check back into your riad. Spend the afternoon revisiting any souks you didn't fully explore, or visit the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech if not visited earlier. Alternatively, take a calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the ramparts of the Medina (~150–200 MAD for 45 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final evening in Djemaa el-Fna — watch the acrobats, henna artists, and musicians. Treat yourself to a nicer farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop in the Atlas Mountains — sandwiches, fruit, and Moroccan pastries from a local bakery (~50–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly at Dar Yacout or Comptoir Darna — atmospheric Moroccan palace dining with live entertainment (~350–500 MAD per person, reservation required)

day_by_day.notes: The Tizi n'Tichka road can be winding — if you're prone to motion sickness, take medication before departure. The drive back to Marrakech takes approximately 4–5 hours with stops. Consider booking your farewell dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Mellah's covered market for last-minute souvenir shopping: argan oil, Moroccan spices (ras el hanout, saffron), leather goods, and handmade ceramics. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (government-fixed prices, no bargaining needed — great for fair-priced quality crafts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, enjoy a final mint tea on a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful final stroll — the minaret is the most iconic landmark in Marrakech. Pack up and arrange your airport transfer (petit taxi ~80–120 MAD or pre-booked transfer ~150–200 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. If you have an evening flight, enjoy one final tagine or pastilla at a café near the Medina before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad — savor one last traditional Moroccan spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Clock Marrakech — a beloved cultural hub serving camel burgers, traditional dishes, and fresh juices in a beautiful courtyard (~130–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Light meal at the airport or a quick stop at a café near the Medina before departure — try a b'stilla (sweet-savory pigeon or chicken pie) as a final Moroccan farewell (~60–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. Keep a small amount of MAD for the taxi to the airport. Morocco's VAT refund is available for purchases over 2,000 MAD at participating shops — ask for the form when shopping.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to your boutique riad in Djemaa el-Fna, Medina. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony hosted by your riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Djemaa el-Fna square — absorb the vibrant atmosphere of snake charmers, musicians, and storytellers. Stroll through the adjacent Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and admire the ornate Saadian Tombs exterior. Visit the nearby Bahia Palace for a first taste of Moroccan architecture and tilework (entry included in private guide package).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from a rooftop terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna — witness the square transform into a magical open-air theatre as dusk falls. Private guided evening walk through the illuminated souks of the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at your riad's private courtyard — traditional Moroccan spread with harira soup, briouats, and fresh salads prepared by the riad's chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin Secret Restaurant or Dar Yacout — one of Marrakech's most celebrated palatial dining experiences featuring bastilla, slow-cooked lamb tagine, and honey pastilla for dessert, set within a stunning 19th-century riad

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Ask your riad concierge to brief you on the week's schedule and confirm all bookings. Carry local dirhams for small tips. Light layers recommended for the March evening breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Medina's historic landmarks: begin at the magnificent Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior), then explore the Ben Youssef Madrasa — a 14th-century Islamic college with breathtaking carved stucco and cedar woodwork. Continue to the Museum of Marrakech housed in a stunning 19th-century palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive private hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Hammam de la Rose — traditional black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage (2–3 hours). Followed by a guided spice market tour in the souks with a master herbalist explaining Moroccan botanicals and traditional remedies.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class at a premium culinary school (e.g., La Maison Arabe Cooking School) — learn to prepare a three-course Moroccan feast including traditional couscous, preserved lemon chicken, and Moroccan pastries under expert guidance.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Moroccan breakfast at your riad — msemen flatbreads, amlou (argan-almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, honey, dates, and Berber omelette
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café des Épices in the spice square — rooftop terrace with panoramic Medina views, fresh salads and Moroccan wraps
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during your cooking class in the school's candlelit dining room, paired with fresh-pressed juices and Moroccan mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam and cooking class at least 48 hours in advance through your riad concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina exploration. The Ben Youssef Madrasa can be crowded — early morning entry is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Atlas Mountains — private luxury 4x4 transfer through the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m). Morning stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a stunning fortified ksar (ancient city) used as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided walk through the labyrinthine earthen towers and granaries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Dades Valley or Ouarzazate region — visit a traditional Berber village, meet a local family for authentic cultural exchange, and explore rose-growing terraces (March is pre-rose season but fields are lush). Optional short hike through the rocky gorge landscape with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Marrakech via scenic mountain route. Sunset cocktails on your riad's rooftop terrace upon return.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast before early departure — traditional Moroccan spread with fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your riad — artisanal sandwiches, Moroccan salads, fresh fruit, and pastries enjoyed with panoramic Atlas Mountain views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with a modern twist, rooftop terrace with stunning views, featuring dishes like lamb mechoui and spiced seafood pastilla

day_by_day.notes: Departure from riad by 07:30 recommended for optimal timing. The mountain roads can be winding — motion sickness tablets advised if sensitive. Dress in layers as Atlas Mountain temperatures can be cooler. Photography opportunities are exceptional along this route.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early (06:00) for the Sahara Desert — a scenic 8–9 hour drive through dramatic southern Moroccan landscapes including the Draa Valley, palm oases, and ancient kasbahs. En-route stop at Skoura Oasis — a vast palm grove with over 700,000 palms and historic fortified ksour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival at Merzouga / Erg Chebbi dunes region. Check into your luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge (e.g., Scarabeo Camp or Kasbah Tombouctou). Private camel trek into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest dunes in Morocco reaching 150 metres.
day_by_day.evening: Magical Sahara sunset atop the dunes with chilled Moroccan tea and dates. Arrive at your exclusive luxury tented camp — enjoy a private Gnawa music performance around a fire under an extraordinary star-filled desert sky. Stargazing session with a local astronomer guide.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at riad — packed to-go or quick sit-down before 06:00 departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet roadside lunch at a premium kasbah restaurant in Boumalne Dades or Tinghir — traditional Berber tagine and fresh salads in a garden setting
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner under the stars at your luxury desert camp — multi-course Moroccan feast with lamb mechoui, Berber couscous, and traditional sweets, served by candlelight in the open desert

day_by_day.notes: The drive is long but spectacularly scenic — consider an overnight stop option if preferred. Bring a warm layer for desert nights (March temperatures can drop to 8–12°C). Confirm luxury camp booking well in advance as premium spots fill up quickly. Closed-toe shoes recommended for dune climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up (05:30) for a private sunrise camel or quad bike ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — witness the Sahara awakening in spectacular golden light. Optional sandboarding on the dunes. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Visit the nearby Merzouga village and the Gnawa community — learn about their ancient sub-Saharan musical heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: 4x4 desert adventure with an expert local guide — explore hidden fossil sites (the region is rich in 400-million-year-old marine fossils), nomadic Berber encampments, and the seasonal salt lake of Dayet Srji (flamingo habitat in season). Optional visit to a local artisan workshop for fossil and mineral crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your luxury desert camp or kasbah lodge. Indulge in a traditional hammam treatment offered at the camp. Private dinner with live Berber music performance.

meals.breakfast: Lavish desert camp breakfast after sunrise — fresh fruit, Moroccan pancakes, honey, argan oil, eggs, and mint tea served in the open air
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp or a local desert village — harira soup, Berber bread, olives, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at your luxury kasbah or desert camp — slow-roasted lamb, saffron-infused couscous, and traditional Moroccan pastries with live Gnawa music accompaniment

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise experience is unmissable — set multiple alarms. Sunscreen and a hat are essential for afternoon desert activities. Stay hydrated throughout the day. If interested in fossil purchases, negotiate respectfully and ensure authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga for the return journey to Marrakech via an alternate scenic northern route through the Todra Gorge — dramatic 300-metre-high rock canyon walls carved by the Todra River. Private guided walk through the gorge floor with a geology and history briefing. Explore the Tinghir palm oasis nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka Pass. Stop at a traditional Berber cooperative for argan oil production demonstration and premium argan product shopping. Arrival back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into your Medina riad and refresh.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private tour of the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum at dusk (private after-hours access if bookable through concierge) — the cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and beloved by Yves Saint Laurent is ethereal in evening light. Followed by a farewell Medina stroll.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast — traditional spread with panoramic dune views before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Tinghir or Boumalne Dades — fresh trout from local rivers (a regional speciality), Berber salads and tagine
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at La Mamounia Hotel's Le Français or Le Marocain restaurant — one of the world's most iconic luxury hotels, offering impeccable French-Moroccan fine dining in a palace setting

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 8 hours — plan for a 07:00 departure. The Todra Gorge is stunning in morning light. La Mamounia dinner reservations must be made well in advance — request through your riad concierge. Smart casual dress code applies at La Mamounia.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — leisurely breakfast at the riad. Private guided shopping tour through the Medina's finest artisan souks: handwoven Berber carpets in the carpet souk, hand-hammered copper lanterns, premium leather goods at the Chouara Tannery viewpoint, and bespoke Moroccan slippers (babouches). Your guide helps with quality assessment and fair price negotiation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace ruins — two of Marrakech's most important historic sites, dating to the 16th-century Saadian dynasty. Enjoy a final relaxed lunch in the Medina. Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Ensemble Artisanal (fixed-price government cooperative — no bargaining required, guaranteed quality).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails on your riad rooftop. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure. End of an extraordinary Moroccan journey.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final riad breakfast — full Moroccan spread with fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen, amlou, honey, dates, and Berber omelette
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Le Tobsil — a legendary Marrakech institution serving an extravagant multi-course Moroccan feast in a 17th-century riad with live Andalusian music
meals.dinner: Light dinner or airport lounge dining depending on departure time — your riad can prepare a gourmet to-go box if needed

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. Keep a small amount of dirhams for final tips to riad staff (customary and appreciated). Ensure all purchased goods are properly packed — fragile items like ceramics and glassware need careful wrapping. Confirm airport transfer the evening before.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026
